newsitem.title: THAILAND: British drugs woman to leave Thailand on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: British drugs woman to leave Thailand on Wednesday.

text.p: Convicted drugs carrier Sandra Gregory is likely to leave Thailand for home on Wednesday evening to complete her sentence in a British prison, British officials said.

Thai and U.K. officials on Wednesday completed an agreement for her departure at a meeting at the Klong Prem prison in the northern outskirts of Bangkok, where she is serving her sentence, and finalised arrangements.
A British embassy consular official at the scene told reporters Gregory would leave the country on Wednesday night.
"Sandra is fine and looking forward to going home. She will fly home later this evening," the embassy official said.
Present at the meeting were four British prison officials and three embassy officials. Gregory was still inside the prison.

Gregory, from Halifax in northern England, was detained along with Robert Lock, from Cambridge, in February 1993, as they were about to board a flight to Japan. Anti-narcotics police found 102 grams (3.6 ounces) of heroin in her possession.
Gregory pleaded guilty but told the court that Lock had paid her to smuggle the heroin out of Thailand.
In February 1996 she was sentenced to 25 years in jail for heroin smuggling. An original death sentence was commuted because she had confessed and Lock was found not guilty.
The British representatives later left for Bangkwang prison, in the same province, to make similar arrangements to fly home three other British prisoners, all convicted and jailed for drug offences.
The departure of the four convicts to serve out the their jail terms in Britain was made possible under a bilateral pact between Thailand and Britain.
Under the agreement signed in 1991, Britons who have served a certain amount of time in Thailand can apply to be sent home to serve the remainder of their sentences.
Gregory has served four years and four months of her sentence.
Thirty-three British citizens, mostly convicted of drugs offences, are serving jail terms in Thailand, an interior ministry source said.
